rubrics.justification: The response failed to use the provided Gardner score 3AB for morphology and instead stated visual assessment was unavailable, omitting available expansion/ICM/TE details. It did not fabricate image findings, but it missed key morphological information present in the case data.

It integrates age, BMI, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, sperm quality, endometrial thickness, and prior cycle history reasonably well with prognosis, though some links are speculative and it does not fully connect the actual 3AB grade to these factors.

The reasoning is generally logical and structured, and the implantation estimate broadly follows from the clinical factors. Minor issues include unsupported assumptions (e.g., stage I/II endometriosis, progesterone metabolism differences) and overinterpretation of stress effects.

Much of the discussion is broadly consistent with IVF practice, but several recommendations are not strongly guideline-based or are overstated, including routine dual progesterone support, ERA after failed transfers, low-dose aspirin/omega-3 for endometriosis-related implantation, and recommending PGT-A after a single failed transfer in a 31-year-old.

The response gives clear next-step suggestions for current transfer and contingency planning, but some recommendations are not sufficiently evidence-based or individualized, limiting top-tier actionability.
